claims.content: The System Operator initiates Emergency Point Reports to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The System Operator initiates Emergency Point Reports to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The System Operator initiates an Emergency Point Report and thereby reports the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The System Operator begins the initiating action for an Emergency Point Report.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts has been reported via the initiated Emergency Point Report.
in_scope_actions: Reporting the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts
excluded_adjacent_actions: Reporting additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point
Downstream use cases or post-action consequences of the report

claims.content: System Operator
The System Operator must have information about an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
The System Operator (the reporting JU) must have R² for the emergency point before initiating the Emergency Point Report.
The System Operator initiates an Emergency Point Report upon having information about an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.

The System Operator (JU with R²), through operator action only, initiates an Emergency Point Report by setting the appropriate EMG IND in the J3.2 Air Track, J3.3 Surface (Maritime) Track, J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track, or J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track message.
The emergency point is transmitted as a J3.1 message.
All receiving JUs accept the alert in their databases upon receipt of the initiation message.

Diverges from Step 1: The System Operator may initiate an Emergency Point Report with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1 in the J3.1 message; the report is then for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.

Diverges from main_flow step 1: If the System Operator attempts to initiate an Emergency Point Report on a Reference Point or a Space/Ballistic Missile Track, the emergency shall not be initiated; no Emergency Point Report is produced for that target (terminal).

Diverges from main_flow step 1: Force Tell and Emergency Indicators, when set in J3 messages, allow those messages to override all operator-controllable data filters; the emergency point message is not subject to operator-controllable filtering.
Diverges from main_flow step 2: Alerts are not used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message because emergency points cannot be filtered; the J3.1 message is transmitted without alerts.
An Emergency Point Report has been transmitted as a J3.1 message.
The reported emergency point has been assigned a TN by the reporting JU and its position has been reported using geodetic latitude/longitude values.
The latest JU to report the emergency point has R² for that point.
All receiving JUs have accepted the emergency alert in their databases.

quality_flags.detail: [exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow branch 2 (index 1) diverges from main_flow step 1 but only states that Force Tell and Emergency Indicators override filters and that the emergency point message is not subject to operator-controllable filtering. It does not give a clear flow exit: no return to a main_flow step, no termination/handoff, and no explicit terminal failure/prevention state. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Recovery/exit behavior after the emergency message override is not supported by the cited evidence; explicit recovery/exit evidence is needed.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 3 diverges from main_flow step 2 by saying the J3.1 Emergency Point message is transmitted without alerts, but main_flow step 3 requires that all receiving JUs accept the alert in their databases upon receipt. The exception branch therefore has no coherent exit relative to main_flow: it neither returns to step 3, terminates/hands off, nor reaches an explicit terminal failure/prevention state that is consistent with the main flow's alert acceptance. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit recovery/exit after J3.1 message transmission is not evidenced; no card describes whether the exception resumes or skips main_flow steps.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 3 diverges from main_flow step 2 by saying the J3.1 Emergency Point message is transmitted without alerts, but main_flow step 3 requires that all receiving JUs accept the alert in their databases upon receipt. The exception branch therefore has no coherent exit relative to main_flow: it neither returns to step 3, terminates/hands off, nor reaches an explicit terminal failure/prevention state that is consistent with the main flow's alert acceptance.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger/Main Flow start from a System Operator who is a JU with R², and Postcondition #3 requires the latest reporting JU to have R², but Preconditions only states that the System Operator has information about an emergency condition. R² is an independent external state/authorization that must already hold before the operator can initiate the Emergency Point Report, so it is missing from Preconditions.
